studies.Population: Postmenopausal women enrolled in the Women's Health Initiative Observational Study (WHI-OS)
studies.Ethnicity Basis: Default: no protocol-mapped specific country or population was established
studies.Reference: Association of Artificially Sweetened Beverage Consumption and Urinary Tract Cancers in the Women's Health Initiative Observational Study.
studies.Authors: Ringel NE, Hovey KM, Andrews CA, Mossavar-Rahmani Y, Shadyab AH, Snetselaar LG, Howard BV, Iglesia CB
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: The question regarding ASBs was as follows: “During the past 3 mo, how often did you drink these beverages?” (Beverages refer to “diet drinks such as Diet Coke or diet fruit drinks,” with a 12 fl. oz. can as a reference serving size.)

sample_size.excerpt: In this secondary analysis of the Women’s Health Initiative Observational Study that included 80 388 postmenopausal women, higher consumption of artificially sweetened beverages was associated with a higher risk of kidney cancer.

effect_size.excerpt: The association between ASB consumption and incidence of ureter and other urinary organ cancers was not assessed due to small numbers of participants in each group. comparison.excerpt: The frequency of artificially sweetened beverage consumption was categorized as follows: rare artificially sweetened beverage consumption (never to fewer than one serving per week), frequent consumption (one to six servings per week), and daily consumption (more than one servings per day).

design.excerpt: This was a secondary analysis of data from the Women’s Health Initiative Observational Study, a multicenter longitudinal prospective study of the health of 93 676 postmenopausal women with a mean follow-up time of 13.5 yr.

timing.excerpt: The WHI-OS is a prospective, multicenter cohort study of 93 676 postmenopausal women.

continent.excerpt: Women were identified at 40 clinical centers across the USA and enrolled from 1993 to 1998.

studies.Title: Artificial sweetener use and bladder cancer: a case-control study.
studies.Reference: Artificial sweetener use and bladder cancer: a case-control study.
studies.Population: Bladder cancer patients and matched hospital patient controls
studies.comparison_type: Artificial sweetener/diet beverage users vs non-users (also quantity and duration of use)

extraction_supporting_text.cases: In a case-control study of 302 male and 65 female bladder cancer patients and an equal number of other patients matched to them in age, sex, hospital, and hospital-room status, no association was found between use of artificial sweeteners or diet beverages and bladder cancer.
extraction_supporting_text.comparison: no association was found between use of artificial sweeteners or diet beverages and bladder cancer
extraction_supporting_text.design: In a case-control study of 302 male and 65 female bladder cancer patients
extraction_supporting_text.timing: No dose-response was observed with respect to quantity or duration of use of the two combined.
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_measurement: use of artificial sweeteners or diet beverages
extraction_supporting_text.gender: 302 male and 65 female bladder cancer patients

studies.Title: Associations between bladder cancer risk factors and tumor stage and grade at diagnosis.
studies.Reference: Associations between bladder cancer risk factors and tumor stage and grade at diagnosis.
studies.Population: Bladder cancer cases and population-based controls from the National Bladder Cancer Study
studies.comparison_type: Heavy artificial sweetener use versus lower/no use

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: Using data on 1,860 bladder cancer cases and 3,934 population-based controls from the National Bladder Cancer Study, we examined associations between suspected bladder cancer risk factors and tumor stage and grade.
extraction_supporting_text.cases: Using data on 1,860 bladder cancer cases and 3,934 population-based controls from the National Bladder Cancer Study, we examined associations between suspected bladder cancer risk factors and tumor stage and grade.
extraction_supporting_text.comparison: Heavy artificial sweetener use was associated with higher-grade, poorly differentiated tumors.
extraction_supporting_text.design: 1,860 bladder cancer cases and 3,934 population-based controls from the National Bladder Cancer Study
extraction_supporting_text.ethnicity: Compared with whites, nonwhites were at a lower risk of noninvasive bladder cancer
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_measurement: Heavy artificial sweetener use was associated with higher-grade, poorly differentiated tumors.
